title: Water Sampling onto Filters for Nucleic Acids Sequencing
author: Melissa B Duhaime
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jegcjbw

steps.title: Pre-filter the water
steps.instruction: Pre-filter water using a 20 µm mesh net and collect it in a clean carboy. Collect several liters of <20 µm-filtered water; if filtering 1 L in triplicate (3 L total), collect at least 5 L to ensure sufficient volume for system flushing.

steps.title: Assemble and flush the first filtration unit
steps.instruction: Set up the system so flow moves from water source, through pump head, through first filtration unit, through second filtration unit, and into a collection receptacle.

substeps.instruction: Attach tubing to both ends of a 47 mm filter unit and run tubing through the pump head.
Disassemble the unit, leaving the downstream part (where the filter is placed) detached.
Pump approximately 200 ml of <20 µm-filtered water through the system to clean it.
Place a 3 µm filter into the filter unit and close it, ensuring all O-rings are in place to prevent leaks.

steps.title: Assemble and flush the second filtration unit
steps.instruction: Attach the second filtration unit to the first.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble the second filtration unit so only the top half is connected to the system.
Pump approximately 200 ml of <20 µm-filtered water through the system to clean it.
Replace the 3 µm filter (save the first filter for later cleaning of the set-up).
Place a 0.22 µm filter into the second filter unit and close it.

steps.title: Filter the water sample
steps.instruction: Pump 1 liter of water through the system at a moderate rate to avoid high pressure. Collect the flow-through in a graduated waste collection bottle to measure the volume.

substeps.instruction: If the collection rate slows or pressure builds before 1 L is filtered, stop the pump and replace the filters (starting with the 3 µm filter).
If multiple filters are used to reach 1 L, note this for downstream processing.

steps.title: Collect and store filters
steps.instruction: Stop the pump and remove the 3 µm and 0.22 µm filters using sterile tweezers.

substeps.instruction: Place the filters inside a cryovial, using two pairs of tweezers to roll or fold the filter to avoid wrinkling.
Immediately drop the cryovial containing the filters into liquid nitrogen (LN2).

steps.title: Clean the system
steps.instruction: Clean the tubing and filtration units between stations (or flush with station water if full cleaning is not logistically possible).

substeps.instruction: Remove all filters from the units.
Pump approximately 0.50 L of 10% bleach through the tubing and assembled filtration units; collect the outgoing bleach for future pump cleaning.
Pump approximately 1-2 L of Deionized water (or MilliQ) through the pump until the system no longer smells of bleach.
